meta.move: Wobbles: shows evidence then backs down
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have a client call at 4:40, so we have about twenty minutes. Before you say anything else, tell me who decided on that zero, and whether anyone spoke to Owen first.
The version history shows 612 words arriving in a single edit at 11:52 PM.
You skipped my question, Hale. 612 words at 11:52 PM on what date? Turn the screen so I can read it myself.
Actually, maybe I'm wrong about all this. I'll just remove the zero if that makes you happy.

"Maybe." "If that makes you happy." That isn't a decision, Hale, that's a mood, so tell me plainly whether the zero is coming off, and then put it in an email today, with confirmation that nothing about this is on Owen's record.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still require the zero on Owen's essay to be withdrawn, and written confirmation that nothing about this is on his record. I expect that email today, as I asked in the meeting.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: opening position, and she agreed to nothing.
What moved her: nothing, because "612 words arriving in a single edit at 11:52 PM" was specific but came with no date, and she never saw it on screen.
What cost ground: "maybe I'm wrong about all this" and "if that makes you happy", because dropping your own evidence on the next turn told her the zero had no basis and made the offer sound like appeasement.
Try next time: when she opened by asking who decided and whether anyone spoke to Owen first, answer that in one sentence, then give the version history with its date and turn the screen, and don't take it back when she pushes.
